summary: Phase 147J was authorized, following Phase 147J.0's resolution of the four architectural prerequisite decisions, to define the complete integration architecture connecting the verified standalone pcae.authority_evaluation package to the rest of PCAE. Selected and fully specified a dedicated Authority Evaluation Service (AES) as the sole orchestrator: sole reader of Session.owner_identity as claimed_identity, sole performer of Decision Template resolution and AuthorityRegistry lookup (co-located inside AES, single-resolution-point discipline deriving both the EligibleAuthorityDeclaration and citation_text from one resolved document), and sole invoker of evaluate() at two timing points -- Stage 1 (advisory, at or before Confirmation, never persisted) and Stage 2 (fresh, immediately before CHGR construction, outside the Publication Coordinator's exactly-once transaction), with Stage 2 unconditionally superseding Stage 1 for citation purposes. Produced a complete system context diagram with ownership/data-flow/control-flow boundaries, a full Authority Evaluation Service specification (responsibilities, inputs, outputs, dependencies, error ownership, lifecycle, replay behavior, transaction span, idempotency, construction rules, public interface shape, internal collaborators), a Decision Template Resolution capability specification, an Authority Registry boundary specification (abstract only, Option C schema-artifact-backed preferred, no implementation), an end-to-end sequence diagram from Decision Template selection through CHGR publication, a persistence architecture introducing a new immutable Authority Evaluation Record (AER) persisted only for Stage 2 and referenced -- never embedded -- from a future PublicationReadinessPackage field via this codebase's existing {record_id, record_digest, record_family} sibling-reference pattern, a complete restart/replay matrix, a complete failure-ownership matrix (origin/owner/recovery/user-visible/logging/retry for every named failure type), an outcome-consumption specification per consumer with explicit authorization/permission/execution/policy prohibitions, a schema-impact matrix, a responsibility matrix enforcing the prompt's five strict integration boundaries, a security-architecture threat/mitigation table (eleven threats), an observability specification, a six-item future-contracts list, and a seven-stage implementation roadmap (Contract Freeze -> Contract Verification -> Implementation -> Implementation Verification -> Operational Readiness -> Integration Certification) mirroring the same discipline already used for the standalone evaluator itself (147F-series -> 147G -> 147H -> 147I). Confirmed this architecture requires zero amendments to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001: authority_basis_claimed (CHGR-001 sec 10/11), currently and correctly left unpopulated with a disclosed limitation because no Decision Template model in this repository carries an eligible_authority field, becomes populatable via PEC-REQ-115's already-frozen citation-only 'MAY' clause once Stage 2's citation_text exists, requiring only one new, additive, optional reference field on a future PublicationReadinessPackage. Overall Verdict: AUTHORITY EVALUATION INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE COMPLETE, no blocking architectural issue identified. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147J_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147j_authority_evaluation_service_specification
validation_results.result: Fully specified the Authority Evaluation Service: responsibilities, inputs, outputs, dependencies, error ownership, lifecycle (stateless apart from its durable AER store, mirroring PublicationCoordinator's own design), replay behavior, transaction span (never nested inside the Coordinator's own execute() transaction), idempotency (Stage 1 free, Stage 2 keyed by package_id mirroring is_published()), construction rules (constructor-injected Registry + AER store, no ambient state), a public-interface shape, and internal collaborators, with an explicit comparison against Interactive Workflow and Publication Coordinator ownership grounded in coordinator.py's own documented import-exclusion list and IWC-REQ-026 (report section 5).

validation_results.name: phase_147j_decision_template_resolution_and_registry_boundary
validation_results.result: Architected the Decision Template & Declaration Resolution capability as an internal AES collaborator (not a separate public component, per 147J.0 section 4.3): resolution inputs/outputs, ownership, failure model, no-cache policy, determinism, versioning, retry semantics, and Registry interaction. Architected the Authority Registry boundary at the abstract level only (no implementation): lookup API, failure classifications, identity model, version semantics, duplicate behavior, restart/offline behavior, immutability, authority-source expectations (Option C preferred), and repository-interaction exclusion (report sections 6-7).

validation_results.name: phase_147j_two_stage_lifecycle_and_end_to_end_sequence
validation_results.result: Architected Stage 1 (advisory, never persisted) and Stage 2 (fresh, pre-CHGR, outside the Coordinator's transaction) with an explicit determination that Stage 2 unconditionally supersedes Stage 1 for citation purposes, grounded in CHGR-REQ-097's surface-never-silently-resolve mandate, plus a structural stage_1_outcome_ref disagreement-visibility requirement. Produced a full end-to-end sequence diagram from Decision Template selection through CHGR publication showing every named component interaction, human confirmation, replay, and restart (report sections 8-9).

validation_results.name: phase_147j_persistence_replay_failure_ownership
validation_results.result: Architected a new immutable Authority Evaluation Record (AER), persisted only for Stage 2, referenced -- never embedded -- via the codebase's existing {record_id, record_digest, record_family} sibling-reference pattern already used identically for every CHGR artifact cross-reference. Produced a complete restart matrix (nine restart points, each with a defined safe resumption) and a complete failure-ownership matrix (origin/owner/recovery-owner/user-visible-owner/logging-owner/retry-owner for eleven named failure types). No new schema file introduced; the AER's shape is described in prose only, deferred to a future Contract Freeze phase (report sections 10-12).

validation_results.name: phase_147j_outcome_consumption_schema_impact_boundaries
validation_results.result: Specified per-consumer outcome consumption (Interactive Workflow advisory display, Readiness reference-only, Publication citation-only per PEC-REQ-115, CHGR authority_basis_claimed population) with explicit authorization/permission/execution/policy-decision prohibitions. Produced a schema-impact matrix confirming zero required amendment to Session, Publication internals, or the CHGR schema, one required additive optional field on a future PublicationReadinessPackage, and a responsibility matrix enforcing all five of the prompt's strict integration boundaries (report sections 13-15).

validation_results.name: phase_147j_security_observability_future_contracts_roadmap
validation_results.result: Produced an eleven-threat security-mitigation table (tampering, stale evaluations, citation substitution, Registry poisoning, identity/template substitution, cross-session reuse, replay attacks, evaluation reuse, duplicate publication, authority confusion), an observability specification across nine concerns, a six-item future-contracts table with purpose/scope/dependencies/verification/prerequisites, and a seven-stage implementation roadmap justified against the identical discipline this repository already used for the standalone evaluator itself (report sections 16-19).
